speaker: Doctor
text: That mechanism suggests a potential ligament injury, often called a "jammed finger" or collateral ligament sprain. Can you tell me if you have any difficulty bending or straightening the finger, or if it feels unstable when you try to grip objects?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. speaker: Doctor
text: Your symptoms are highly suggestive of a mallet finger, where the extensor tendon is disrupted at the distal interphalangeal joint. I will order an X-ray to confirm if there is any associated fracture before finalizing the treatment plan. REQUEST TEST: X-Ray_Right_Finger

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray rules out a fracture, confirming this is a pure tendon injury. Based on the mechanism and inability to actively extend the DIP joint, this is a classic mallet finger. DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
